verses.text: "'This is what the Lord GOD says: The gate of the inner courtyard that faces east must stay shut on the six working days, but it must be opened on the Sabbath day and on the day of the New Moon.

The prince is to come in from outside through the porch of the gateway and stand by the gatepost. The priests will offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he will worship at the threshold of the gateway. Then he will go out, but the gate must not be shut until evening.
On the Sabbaths and New Moons, the people of the land are to worship before the LORD at the entrance of that gateway.
The burnt offering the prince brings to the LORD on the Sabbath day is to be six lambs and one ram, all with nothing wrong with them.
The grain offering with the ram is to be one ephah, and with the lambs it is to be as much as he wants to give, along with a hin of olive oil for each ephah.
On the day of the New Moon, he is to offer a young bull, six lambs, and a ram, all with nothing wrong with them.
He is to provide a grain offering of one ephah with the bull and one ephah with the ram, and with the lambs as much as he wants to give, along with a hin of olive oil for each ephah.
When the prince comes in, he is to enter through the porch of the gateway and leave the same way.

"'When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed festivals, whoever comes in through the north gate to worship must go out through the south gate. Whoever comes in through the south gate must go out through the north gate. No one may go back out through the gate they came in. Each person must go straight out the opposite side.
The prince is to be among them, going in when they go in and going out when they go out.

"'At the festivals and appointed feasts, the grain offering is to be one ephah with each bull and one ephah with each ram, and with the lambs as much as he wants to give, along with a hin of olive oil for each ephah.

When the prince gives a voluntary offering to the LORD, whether a burnt offering or peace offerings, the gate facing east is to be opened for him. He is to offer his burnt offering or his peace offerings just as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he will go out, and after he has gone out, the gate is to be shut.
"'Every day you must provide a one-year-old lamb with nothing wrong with it as a burnt offering to the LORD. Provide it every morning.

With it, every morning, you must also provide a grain offering of one sixth of an ephah of fine flour with one third of a hin of olive oil to moisten it. This grain offering to the LORD is a lasting rule that must always be kept.
So the lamb, the grain offering, and the olive oil must be provided every morning as a regular burnt offering.
"'This is what the Lord GOD says: If the prince gives a gift from his land to one of his sons, it will belong to his descendants. It is their property by inheritance.
But if he gives a gift from his land to one of his servants, the servant may keep it only until the year of freedom. Then it goes back to the prince. His inheritance belongs only to his sons.

The prince must not take any of the people's inheritance and drive them off their property. He must give his sons their inheritance from his own property, so that none of my people will be driven off their land.'"
Then the man brought me through the entrance at the side of the gate into the holy rooms of the priests that faced north. He showed me a place at the far west end.

He said to me, "This is where the priests will boil the guilt offerings and the sin offerings and bake the grain offerings. That way they will not have to bring them into the outer courtyard and make the people holy."
Then he brought me out into the outer courtyard and led me around to its four corners. In each corner I saw another small courtyard.
In the four corners of the outer courtyard were enclosed courtyards, forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. All four were the same size.
Each of the four had a stone ledge around it, with fireplaces built under the ledges all around.
He said to me, "These are the kitchens where those who serve in the temple will boil the people's sacrifices."
